Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Coral and Japanese honeysuckles

The catalogue treats coral honeysuckle and introduced Japanese honeysuckle as separate plants. It records aromatic and medicinal traditions and describes how Japanese honeysuckle became part of local practice.1

The Point woodland reference is printed beside coral honeysuckle; the introduced honeysuckle is described much more broadly.1

Places named in the catalogue

The Point; Shinnecock territories.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF p. 22. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
